articles.title: Destiny Isn’t Dead After All, Bungie Admits It Lost Sight Of What Players Loved
articles.summary: Bungie has admitted that it "lost sight" of what players loved about its games over the past few years, acknowledging that a series of broken promises and shifting promises caused the studio to lose the trust of its community.
body: In a new video accompanied by a blog post on the Bungie website, Bungie studio head Poria Torkan and Marathon head of product and general manager Josh Dean addressed the studio's recent struggles and outlined its plans for the future. Torkan acknowledges that Bungie's ambitions had stalled as the studio pursued too many different initiatives without enough focus on the things players actually want.
"We lost trust. We lost incredible colleagues. And our ambitions as a studio stalled," Torkan said. "We chased vision without enough focus on what players loved, and that's on us. We own that."

Bungie directly acknowledged the frustration surrounding Destiny 2--which received its last content update on June 9, 2026--including the removal of large amounts of content from the game in "sunsetting" processes.
"We haven't just heard your feedback. We understand the anger, the disappointment with us," Torkan said. "We're not asking for your trust, we know we have to earn it."

articles.summary: Nintendo's latest September Direct had quite an exciting announcement for fans of Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2: the game is getting a Royal Edition on Nintendo Switch 2 next year.
body: As of the time of writing, it appears only Amazon has the new Switch 2 edition up to preorder, but we'll be keeping an eye out for other retailers as they drop their preorder pages over time. It's worth mentioning that this version of the game on Nintendo Switch 2 comes as a Game-key card. That means the game is not included on the cartridge. Putting the cartridge in your Switch 2 lets you download and play the game. However, unlike a digital game, you can sell this one.

It was one of our favorite video games of 2025 - and even a contender for our selection of the best RPG of last year - with reviewer Len Hafer giving it a 9/10 score and writing: "Armed with excellent melee combat and an exceptional story, Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 is one part sequel and one part coronation, bringing a lot of the original's ideas to fruition."

articles.title: Bungie Bosses Promise to ‘Evolve’ Marathon, Deny Game Will ‘Replace’ Destiny
articles.summary: Bungie Studio Head Poria Torkan and Josh Dean, Head of Product and GM of Marathon, revealed plans to “evolve” Marathon as Bungie continues to navigate big internal changes.
body: In a September 21 video message to fans, Torkan and Dean addressed what’s next for Marathon, saying the game is an “important part” of shaping where Bungie goes next.
"It didn’t reach as many players as we’d hoped,” Torkan admitted. “But we also know and understand that the game needs to evolve.”

“We’re gonna anchor on what makes Marathon special and evolve it beyond the genre constraints that we’ve placed on it. We’re going to expand Marathon into a deeper survival experience that gives players more ways to take on its dangerous alien world,” Dean continued.

He outlined the team's goal for Marathon by the end of year one, saying that Bungie hopes to "preserve what you already love, but find ways to provide players with more agency in how you play, whether in PvE or PvP."

articles.title: Wolverine Dev Denies Using GenAI After Weird-Looking In-Game Sign Discovered
articles.summary: Fans recently discovered an odd-looking bathroom sign in Marvel's Wolverine, prompting people to wonder if developer Insomniac Games used generative AI. According to Insomniac's community and marketing director James Stevenson, that's a bunch of baloney.
body: Insomniac's last game, 2023's Spider-Man 2, utilized machine-learning to help speed up development, and the company intends to keep doing this going forward. But for now, it sounds like AI-generated assets are off limits.
Marvel's Wolverine released on September 15 and became a swift success, reportedly exceeding the lifetime sales of Death Stranding 2 on PS5 right out of the gate.

While Marvel's Wolverine might not have featured any AI-created assets, that's not the case for every game. Activision's Call of Duty games use generative AI, as does Sega's upcoming Crazy Taxi: World Tour.
GameSpot's Marvel's Wolverine review scored the game an 8/10. Reviewer Tamoor Hussain said of the game, "At best, it’s a fun but forgettable experience that’ll entertain you for a few hours."

articles.title: Bungie Says More Destiny Is Coming, Months After Ending Support for Destiny 2
articles.summary: Bungie has said it is "absolutely not done with Destiny" just months after the controversial decision to end ongoing support for Destiny 2. The five-minute upload features Bungie studio head Poria Torkan and head of product, GM of Marathon Josh Deane.
body: "We're not asking for your trust," Torkan said, acknowledging some of Bungie's recent struggles. "We know we have to earn it, and to do that, we need our games to deliver in ways that exceed your expectations of what you've come to love about the games that we make – and that starts with Destiny.

"Bungie wouldn't be what it is today without it. It's the foundation upon which everything else rests, and we are absolutely not done with Destiny. We have more stories to tell, but we have to do it right and give our teams the time they need to do justice to this amazing universe."

Deane clarified that Bungie's goal is to "return Destiny to its original promise." That means going back to "all-inspiring mystery, the sense of discovery, and the promise of a community of Guardians rallying together, raging against impossible odds."

It's been a painful few months for the players who stuck by Destiny and Destiny 2 before substantial support came to an end with the Monument of Triumph update in June. Unfortunately, restoring that community and rebuilding trust will take even more time.

articles.title: Pokemon Is Celebrating Space Week With Cool Merch, And You Just Know Scalpers Will Ruin It
articles.summary: World Space Week kicks off on October 4, and if the idea of exploring the infinite horizon of the cosmos doesn't interest you, then maybe a world-famous Pokemon can inspire you to reach for the stars.
body: Back on terra firma, there'll be exhibitions at ESA facilities during ESA Open Days, and at museums during World Space Week. This will cover France, Italy, Germany, Spain, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom.

While the goal is to both educate and entertain the next generation of explorers, there's a good chance that exclusive collaboration products will also be a big draw. These will include plushies, Pokemon Trading Card Game accessories, and a replica of Adenot's Pikachu decked out in astronaut gear and a bomber jacket. The ESA online shop will also offer special Pikachu-themed ESA apparel, including T-shirts, a tote bag, a notepad, and pins.

And that's cool! It's also likely to attract the seedier side of the Pokemon fandom, as we've seen several times in the past, as just about everything with Pokemon branding is usually scooped up by scalpers and sold online to collectors who couldn't get their hands on those items. In one notable example, chaos broke out during a special exhibit at the Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam after people flocked to acquire a limited-edition Pikachu card, which ended with four workers being fired for alleged misconduct.

articles.title: Physint Is Biggest-Selling Game Kojima Could Ever Make, He Says
articles.summary: Gaming legend Hideo Kojima was recently in the news when it was announced that Sony had dropped his new spy game Physint, with Xbox swooping in to sign it. In the aftermath of the shocking announcement, more information has come to light, including how Kojima thought Physint had major commercial…
body: He told The Washington Post, "This is the biggest selling title I could possibly create." He went on to say, as reported by Kotaku, "I didn't think Physint would be on the list of being canceled."

According to veteran gaming reporter Jason Schreier, Sony abandoned Physint after Kojima Productions reportedly went over budget and missed deadlines. In response, Kojima Productions said people should be skeptical of what they read on the internet, though the Japanese studio did not refute the details of the report.
In an interview with IGN, Kojima said Physint is still in the concept phase. He is working out the game's systems, visuals, and design, and added that a "very small team" is working on it right now.
Despite this, Kojima believes a game like Physint has a lot of appeal because, "Anything espionage is going to be fun, period, no matter what game it is."

articles.title: Bungie is freeing vaulted Destiny 2 campaigns after Marathon "did not reach as many players as we had hoped"
articles.summary: Bungie's been having a tough time these past few years, but the studio's new leadership is making big promises. Starting with Destiny 2 - the devs will start to let some of the game's older campaigns and raids out of the vault, while trying to build a future for the popular MMO-FPS hybrid.
body: "Bungie has been creating games for over 30 years and we have welcomed the communities that have formed around them. Over the last few years, we lost sight of that, and there have been real consequences. We lost trust, we lost incredible colleagues, and we lost sight of what we should be prioritizing most, our players," studio head Poria Torkan and head of product Josh Deane said in today's online statement. The duo then acknowledged fans probably won't start trusting "what we say today," but they're making moves to improve both Destiny and Marathon, regardless.

For context, earlier this year, Bungie laid off at least 290 employees shortly after waving goodbye to Destiny 2 with a final update. The studio's Marathon reboot hasn't been popular enough to fill the hole left by Destiny's absence, either. At the time, reports claimed there were no Destiny-related projects in active development, Destiny 3 included.
points: Bungie's been having a tough time these past few years, but the studio's new leadership is making big promises.

articles.title: Where to find paradise fish in Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave
articles.summary: To find the rare paradise fish in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, you will need to explore distant areas that will take you away from the safety of Dagsion — a risk you must take if you plan on recruiting Ninae.
body: This is the case with this unique fish, but in this guide, we help you locate it by pointing out where to find paradise fish in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave.

Paradise fish is a rare material that you can only find in Lake Brontes, a fishing node on the south side of Saveilon. You should have a party of characters around level 25 to traverse this region without too much trouble in case enemies appear in your path.

Since paradise fish is the rarest material in the Lake Brontes node, you might need more than one turn using the "Search" command to collect one. You can always save before attempting to gather it, and if you fail, just reload the game. Another option is to leave a battalion to collect materials from that node, but this is only available on Theodora's path.

articles.title: Bungie Officially Bringing Back Destiny in Major Update
articles.summary: Months after ending development on Destiny 2 and laying off most of the development team behind its hit shared-world sci-fi shooter, Bungie is returning to the franchise.
body: That includes unvaulting the game's major content updates and laying the foundation for "new Destiny stories and games."
In a video message from Torkan and Deane, the duo addressed the future of Destiny at Bungie, saying that the studio "wouldn't be what it is today without it."

"It's the foundation upon which everything else rests, and we are absolutely not done with Destiny," Torkan said. "We have more stories to tell, but we have to do it right and give our teams the time they need to do justice to this amazing universe."

"We want to return Destiny to its original promise, to return to awe-inspiring mystery, the sense of discovery, and the promise of a community of Guardians rallying together, raging against impossible odds," added Deane. "But that has to start with restoring what's rightfully yours. It's gonna take some time but we're going to commit to unvaulting the Destiny 2 campaigns, the destinations, [and] the raids, that never should have been ripped away to begin with.

articles.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker getting a new difficulty option, combat changes and more in game's first "big" patch scheduled for early October
articles.summary: Speaking to Eurogamer, The Blood of Dawnwalker game director Konrad Tomaszkiewicz has discussed several game improvements coming in a "big patch" currently scheduled for early October - including a brand new difficulty option, combat targeting changes, and making it easier to escape from battles by…
body: Tomaszkiewicz also told me in an interview that the studio is exploring a New Game Plus mode - "Yes, we are," he said smiling but not saying anything more - and potentially adding new enemies to improve variety. "There is a chance but I don't want to speak about it yet," he said. "We will have the proper beats with our publishing team and if I tell you more, they will kill me."

The game's new difficulty is not a harder difficulty, by the way - Rebel Wolves feels Duelist difficulty, without directional attack indicators, is challenging enough. Instead, it's an easier one - the easiest one. It doesn't have a name yet but it effectively replaces the game's current easiest difficulty, Story mode, and takes that name. The existing Story difficulty will be renamed as a result, so Dawnwalker will have five difficulty levels: Story, Story-renamed, Fair, Challenging, and Duelist.

articles.title: Critical Role's New Daggerheart Campaign Reinvents a Formula That Made D&D History
articles.summary: It’s a great time to be a tabletop role-playing games fan — perhaps even the best time in more than a decade. I’m not just talking about the flourishing TTRPG market, with indie projects getting almost $4 million in funding on their first campaign day, or about the exciting barrage of Dungeons &…
body: Critical Role’s in-house TTRPG launched in May 2025 and immediately sold out. The game has a vast, tight-knit community of players, but unless you’re already part of it or watch Critical Role regularly, it can feel relatively obscure. But that’s by design: Daggerheart lacks D&D’s cross-media promotional power, and it doesn’t care. Quietly, the game is setting out not just to sell out its books, but to revolutionize fantasy TTRPGs as we know them.

One item that did make the news: Back in June 2025, the two designers who shaped D&D’s 5th edition, Chris Perkins and Jeremy Crawford, left Wizards of the Coast to join Critical Role’s publishing arm, Darrington Press. In layperson's terms, this was the equivalent of Shigeru Miyamoto leaving Nintendo for Sony. In the year since, however, both designers have been relatively quiet, except for a handful of interviews and public appearances. It’s a big difference from when they were popping up every day in D&D's Instagram video.

articles.title: Pokémon Scalpers Are Officially Melting Down Over 30th Anniversary TCG Set and It's Glorious
articles.summary: Pokémon collectors who snagged the 30th Anniversary card set over the last week have been delighted to discover the collection's incredible pull rates. Illustration cards are seemingly hiding in every Pokémon box out there, which is a great thing for fans who have spent the last year getting…
body: A wide range of posts hailing from unknown Discord servers have gone viral over the last few days, each one more ridiculous than the last.

"I am pissed," reads one recent unsourced Discord post. "I paid a bunch of local homeless people... to wait in line for the 30th drop. Guaranteed them 50% of profits on all sales or 200 cash per Elite Trainer Box they got... I am losing about $150 per ETB at current prices."

Another oft-cited Discord post begins, "I am seriously considering taking legal action against Pokémon. It's disgusting that they didn't share print numbers, pull rates, and how big the supply truly is... honestly, this could be a RICO violation if we find that they purposefully did this."

Polygon cannot verify if these viral Pokémon posts are authentic. However, as a reporter who is a part of many Pokémon restock Discord servers, they're consistent with sentiments from multiple resellers. Over the last few days, I've witnessed a number of angry people regretting their 30th Anniversary purchases. In one instance, I watched a man spend hours on a Discord server describing how he had been excited about the set until he pulled a Gengar Prime Classic Collection card.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 sleuths are torn on whether a famous Florida locale is in the game or not
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto fans are known for a love of speculation and information sleuthing at this point, and this certainly hasn't changed since Rockstar released the extended gameplay preview for Grand Theft Auto 6. The community's current fixation? Whether or not Key West will be in the game.
body: For months, the most eager among the Grand Theft Auto community have been piecing together whatever clues they can as to what the GTA 6 map looks like. Trailers and leaks in combination have allowed fans to draft a rough idea of what we'll be able to explore come November. However, Key West (or Rockstar's own comedic twist on it) has so far remained unseen.

For those unaware, Key West is the USA's southernmost city, located right on the western tip of a chain of islands known as the Florida Keys. It's a famous spot and a popular tourist destination, leading many to speculate as to how it'll appear in Rockstar's take of the Florida coast.

Questions about Key West's inclusion in GTA 6 have circulated for a while, but the conversation has reignited with the appearance of a map leak which appears to show an early beta version of GTA 6's map. This leak is separate from the CyberLeek posts earlier this summer, which notably did not feature Key West at all. As such, the running theory is that Key West might have been planned but removed later in development.

videos.title: Silent Hill: Townfall Review
videos.summary: Silent Hill: Townfall reviewed by Tristan Ogilvie on PlayStation 5. Also available on PC.
body: "Off the back of the more action-oriented sidestep of 2025’s Silent Hill f, Silent Hill: Townfall feels like Konami’s seminal survival horror series returning to what it does best. Its atmosphere is oppressively ominous, its central mystery is genuinely compelling to unravel and packed with themes that feel fresh, and its army of disfigured demons are exhilarating to both encounter and evade. The CRTV device that spots enemies hidden in your surroundings might slightly diminish the story’s ability to deliver major scares early on, but when Townfall eventually got me, it made sure it got me good. It also has some of the most cleverly designed and challenging puzzles I’ve experienced in any horror game in recent memory, many involving impeccable recreations of technology from yesteryear that really transported me back to its mid-nineties setting. Like the intravenous needle permanently jutting out of its hero’s wrist, Silent Hill: Townfall gives this long running series a welcome shot in the arm."
